business_problem: Static flight-hour tables and usage metrics ignored real-time consumption, causing chronic under-resourcing, limited stock effectiveness, and a reactive sustainment supply chain that could not keep pace with modern combat tempos.
solution_summary: Lockheed Martin uses an in-house AI sustainment stack to replace static flight-hour planning with continuously updated logistics intelligence. Telemetry from sensors embedded on airframes and subsystems, mission-specific operational profiles, and strategic inputs such as projected sortie rates and geopolitical risk indicators are ingested into machine learning models that forecast component demand and retrain as new data arrives. Digital twins simulate subsystem behavior and test repair processes, additive manufactured parts, and software patches before field deployment. Forecast outputs, sensor streams, and contract execution data are stitched together in a digital data fabric and served through a web-based LogC2 dashboard for the F-35, with planned extension to F-22, F-16, and C-130 fleets. In the dashboard, reinforcement learning agents recommend replenishment routes and scenario models support what-if planning and actionable logistics orders.
